correctness.summary: The total variation of the mirror products is the L1 norm of an odd Walsh polynomial. Orthogonality bounds the nonlinear remainder by O(v^(3/2)), while the pure-state distinguishability is sqrt(v)(1+O(v)), proving the uniform local expansion. Sharp Khintchine constants give the local interval. For diffuse finite signal, the exact log-likelihood ratio satisfies a triangular-array CLT with limiting N(v,v), and the product overlap converges to exp(-v/2), yielding the explicit efficiency curve; its monotonicity follows from an elementary hyperbolic-sine inequality.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Smirnov's recent mirror-product theorem proves only an unspecified absolute-constant lower comparison; Haagerup's Khintchine constants and local asymptotic normality are classical prior art. Searches did not locate the uniform mirror-product local identity, the complete sharp weak-signal efficiency interval, or the explicit diffuse finite-signal efficiency curve. An equivalent formulation in older binary-experiment or Riesz-product literature remains the main residual risk, so no novelty is claimed for LAN or Khintchine theory themselves.

value.summary: The result sharpens a new constant-factor Bernoulli-product reduction by identifying its exact weak-signal measurement loss, separating concentrated from diffuse signal geometry, and providing a closed-form efficiency curve from sqrt(2/pi) to one.

limitations: The sharp interval is local in the total squared signal.
The finite-signal curve assumes the largest coordinate tends to zero.
No quantitative convergence rate is claimed for the finite-signal triangular array.
The globally optimal constant in Smirnov's mirror-product theorem is not resolved.
Classical LAN, Gaussian test power, and sharp Khintchine constants are prior art.
Older binary-experiment and Riesz-product literature was not exhaustively inspected.
Independent audit has not been performed.
